title: A human genome is about 750 megabytes raw
summary: About 3 billion base pairs, each one of four letters, take 2 bits each: 6 billion bits, 750 million bytes.

beats.say: A human genome is about three billion letters long.
Each position holds one of four bases.
Four options need exactly two bits.
Three billion letters at two bits each.
Divide by eight bits per byte.
That comes to about seven hundred fifty megabytes.

data.note: one set, raw, 2 bits per base

beats.say: That counts one set of chromosomes.
Most cells carry two sets, so double it.
Letters in, bits out. Plain arithmetic.
Four letters cost two bits each.

facts.claim: One copy of the human genome contains approximately 3 billion base pairs of DNA, and adenine pairs with thymine while cytosine pairs with guanine
facts.note: NHGRI Talking Glossary, Base Pair: approximately 3 billion base pairs; A pairs with T, C with G

facts.claim: The human genome contains approximately 3 billion base pairs spread across 23 pairs of chromosomes, and one complete set of genomic instructions is about 3 billion base pairs
facts.note: NHGRI Human Genome Project FAQ: 'approximately 3 billion of these base pairs' and 'one complete set ... is about 3 billion base pairs'

youtube.hook: A human genome is about 3 billion base pairs. Each base is one of four letters, so 2 bits each: 6 billion bits, about 750 megabytes raw.

instagram.caption: A human genome is about 750 megabytes raw: 3 billion letters, 2 bits each, 8 bits to the byte.

tiktok.caption: A human genome is about 750 MB raw.
